name: 国际象棋
tagline: 经典策略游戏：在自己的王倒下之前将死对方的王。
description: 在浏览器中免费下国际象棋：对战 Stockfish 机器人、与朋友在同一设备上对弈或在线对战，支持棋钟、积分对局和复盘分析。
about: Chess is a strategy game for two players on an 8 × 8 board. Each side starts with sixteen pieces: a king, a queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights and eight pawns. White moves first, and the players take turns moving one piece at a time. The goal is to checkmate the other king: to attack it so that it has no way to escape.

Every piece moves in its own way, and the game grows out of how they work together. Pawns march forward and can become a queen on the far side of the board. Kings can castle with a rook to reach safety, and a pawn that has just moved two squares can be captured in passing. A game can also end in a draw: by stalemate, by agreement, by repeating the same position three times, by fifty moves without a capture or a pawn move, or when neither side has enough pieces left to checkmate.

Here you can play against Stockfish, one of the strongest chess engines, on easy, medium or hard, or choose its level yourself. You can also play with a friend on one device, or online in a private room, a public lobby or a quick match, with the usual bullet, blitz, rapid and classical clocks. Signed-in players can play rated games, and every finished game can be stepped through move by move, with Stockfish's evaluation beside it.
howToPlay: Choose how to play: against a bot, on this device with a friend, or online. White moves first.
Tap or drag a piece to see where it can go, then tap or drop it on a highlighted square.
Kings move one square in any direction, queens any distance in a straight line or diagonal, rooks along lines, bishops along diagonals, and knights in an L shape, jumping over other pieces.
Pawns move one square forward, or two from their starting square, and capture one square diagonally forward. A pawn that reaches the last row becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight of your choice.
Put the other king in check so that no move can save it, and you win. You can also win when your opponent resigns or runs out of time.
controls: Phones and tablets: tap a piece and then a square, or drag the piece there.
Mouse: click or drag. Dots mark every square the chosen piece can move to.
Keyboard: move around the board with the arrow keys, press Enter or Space to pick up a piece, and again to put it down.
Resign, offer a draw and, in casual games, ask to take back a move with the buttons beside the board.
tips: Control the centre early: pawns and pieces on the middle squares reach the most of the board.
Bring out your knights and bishops before moving the same piece twice, and castle to keep your king safe.
Before every move, check what your opponent is threatening: captures, checks and attacks on undefended pieces.
Count the material when you trade: a pawn is worth about 1, a knight or bishop 3, a rook 5 and a queen 9.
In the endgame, the king becomes a strong piece. Bring it towards the centre and help your pawns forward.

faq.question: Is chess free to play?
faq.answer: Yes. kefche is free, has no ads, and you don't need an account to play. Rated games need a free account.

faq.question: What is a rated game?
faq.answer: A rated game changes your rating, a number that shows how strong you play. Ratings use the Glicko-2 system and are kept separately for bullet, blitz, rapid and classical.

faq.question: What happens if I run out of time?
faq.answer: You lose the game, unless your opponent has only their king left, or a king and a single knight or bishop. They can't checkmate with that, so the game is a draw.

faq.question: How strong are the bots?
faq.answer: The bots are Stockfish, set to play weaker on easy and medium. Hard is a tough opponent for most club players, and you can also pick any of its 21 levels yourself.
